correctness.rationale: Rearrangement forces the consecutive-value groups of every ordered-partition face; distinct generating entries make the coordinate differences span the sum-zero tangent space of each block. Every subset is realizable as one block with all other coordinates singleton. If T is a face's tangent space, inputs mapping to its relative interior have the form z+W⁻¹v with z in the face and v in the corresponding normal cone. Since T and W⁻¹T⊥ are complementary (positivity of W), face and cone relative interiors give a full open affine cell. The face-affine equality-constrained minimizer on a block B is y_i−a_i(∑_{j∈B}y_j−γ_B)/∑_{j∈B}a_j; the absolute row sum is 1+(|B|−2)a_i/∑_B a_j for |B|≥2 (zero for singleton blocks). The closed cells cover all inputs by the projection optimality condition, so summing affine bounds along segments yields the global upper bound. A short coordinate-sign perturbation in an open maximizing cell attains it exactly. For each fixed block size one can replace the maximizing row weight by a global maximum A and take the remaining smallest weights; ties do not affect the result. The full block gives the lower metric bound 2−2/n with equality requiring equal weights; the supremum n−1 is approached by divergence of one inverse weight, but all denominators strictly exceed A. For the proper-face example the candidates are 1+100/102, 303/103 and 503/203. value.rationale: The exact coordinate amplification is useful when diagonal losses give differently scaled coordinate penalties but the error budget is per-coordinate. A proper face can defeat the natural prediction from the full affine hull; the formula identifies which subset carries the worst error without enumerating all faces, and quantifies how much the weights matter.
residual_risks: The constant describes worst-case finite input pairs, not their frequency or the behavior under arbitrary nonlinear projection penalties.
